--- title: "Communicate" subtitle: "Introduction to Quarto" author: "Morgan Brucks, CCRP" institute: "University of Kansas Medical Center" date: 2026-07-29 image: "../../images/thumbnails/communicate.png" format: revealjs: theme: [default, "../../styles/styleReveal.scss"] slide-number: true preview-links: auto logo: https://brand.ku.edu/sites/brand/files/styles/wide_col_xl_6/public/images/2020/KUMarksLogo.png footer: "R for Lifestyle and Brain Health (R-LAB)" transition: slide background-transition: fade highlight-style: github code-line-numbers: true code-block-bg: true incremental: false date-format: long embed-resources: true execute: freeze: auto --- ## Learning Objectives By the end of today's session, you should be able to understand: - how Quarto documents are structured - how code and narrative work together - how to render documents into polished outputs - the foundations for reproducible research communication ::: notes Key teaching goal: Communication and reproducibility, not memorization of syntax. Many participants will remember concepts better than commands. ::: ## Communicate **Chapters 28-29** | Chapter | Topic | |----------|-------| | 28 | Quarto | | 29 | Quarto formats | ::: notes R4DS argues that communication is part of data science. Data science is not: Data → Analysis → Done It is: Data → Analysis → Communication → Impact Lucky for you, this section focuses on the technial mechanics of Communication, not the act of conveying your thoughts and ideas to other people. That's up to you and your skills. How many of you have: - copied a figure from R into PowerPoint? - copied a table into Word? - had to recreate a figure months later? - struggled to remember how results were generated? Spend 2-3 minutes discussing. This creates buy-in for reproducibility. Ask: "If nobody understands your work, did the analysis accomplish its goal?" ::: # Chapter 28: Quarto ## Basics **What is Quarto?** A publishing system for creating reproducible documents by combining code, text, and visualizations. **Every Quarto document contains four building blocks:** - **YAML** – document settings (title, author, output) - **Markdown** – narrative text - **Code chunks** – R code that performs analyses - **Rendered output** – tables, figures, and results Example: ````markdown ```text --- title: "Exercise Intervention Results" author: "Morgan Brucks" format: html --- ## Participant Characteristics This report summarizes baseline demographics. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} summary(demographics) ``` ::: ```` ::: {.callout-note} Think of Quarto as a recipe: - YAML tells Quarto what to make. - Markdown explains the story. - Code performs the analysis. - Rendering produces the finished document. ::: ## Editors Quarto provides two ways to edit your documents: the Visual Editor for a word processor-like experience and the Source Editor for writing directly in Markdown. Both produce the same final document, so you can choose the workflow that best fits your needs. **Visual** **Source** ````markdown ## Text formatting *italic* **bold** ~~strikeout~~ `code` superscript^2^ subscript~2~ [underline]{.underline} [small caps]{.smallcaps} ## Headings # 1st Level Header ## 2nd Level Header ### 3rd Level Header ## Lists - Bulleted list item 1 - Item 2 - Item 2a - Item 2b 1. Numbered list item 1 2. Item 2. The numbers are incremented automatically in the output. ## Links and images [linked phrase](http://example.com) ![optional caption text](quarto.png){fig-alt="Quarto logo and the word quarto spelled in small case letters"} ## Tables | First Header | Second Header | |--------------|---------------| | Content Cell | Content Cell | | Content Cell | Content Cell | ```` ## Markdown vs. HTML Both Markdown and HTML can be used to format Quarto documents. **Markdown is the preferred syntax for most writing tasks because it is concise, readable, and easy to maintain.** HTML is available when you need additional formatting or customization. | Feature | Markdown | HTML | |:--------|:---------|:-----| | **Bold** | `**text**` | `text` | | **Italic** | `*text*` | `text` | | **Heading** | `## Heading` | `

Heading

` | | **Bullet List** | `- Item` | `
  • Item
` | | **Numbered List** | `1. Item` | `
  1. Item
` | | **Link** | `[Posit](https://posit.co)` | `Posit` | | **Image** | `![Logo](logo.png)` | `` | **Example: Custom HTML Styling** ```html Important Result ``` Markdown cannot easily apply custom colors or styles, but HTML can. ::: {.callout-note title="Hadley's Philosophy"} **Use Markdown for almost everything.** It is easier to read, write, and collaborate on. Use **HTML only when you need formatting that Markdown doesn't support**, such as custom styling, colors, layouts, or embedded web content. ::: ::: {.callout-tip title="Take-Home Message"} You do **not** need to learn HTML to be productive in Quarto. Markdown covers the vast majority of everyday writing tasks, while HTML is there when you need more control over the appearance of your document. ::: ## Code Chunks Code chunks execute your analysis and insert the results directly into your document. Chunk labels and options help organize your work and control what appears in the final output. **Chunk Labels** Meaningful labels make documents easier to navigate and troubleshoot. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](communicate_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: **Chunk Options** Chunk options control **what your audience sees**, not what your code does. | Option | Purpose | |---------|---------| | `echo: false` | Hide code, show results | | `eval: false` | Show code, don't run it | | `warning: false` | Hide warnings | | `message: false` | Hide package messages | Example: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` carat cut color clarity depth Min. :0.2000 Fair : 1610 D: 6775 SI1 :13065 Min. :43.00 1st Qu.:0.4000 Good : 4906 E: 9797 VS2 :12258 1st Qu.:61.00 Median :0.7000 Very Good:12082 F: 9542 SI2 : 9194 Median :61.80 Mean :0.7979 Premium :13791 G:11292 VS1 : 8171 Mean :61.75 3rd Qu.:1.0400 Ideal :21551 H: 8304 VVS2 : 5066 3rd Qu.:62.50 Max. :5.0100 I: 5422 VVS1 : 3655 Max. :79.00 J: 2808 (Other): 2531 table price x y Min. :43.00 Min. : 326 Min. : 0.000 Min. : 0.000 1st Qu.:56.00 1st Qu.: 950 1st Qu.: 4.710 1st Qu.: 4.720 Median :57.00 Median : 2401 Median : 5.700 Median : 5.710 Mean :57.46 Mean : 3933 Mean : 5.731 Mean : 5.735 3rd Qu.:59.00 3rd Qu.: 5324 3rd Qu.: 6.540 3rd Qu.: 6.540 Max. :95.00 Max. :18823 Max. :10.740 Max. :58.900 z Min. : 0.000 1st Qu.: 2.910 Median : 3.530 Mean : 3.539 3rd Qu.: 4.040 Max. :31.800 ``` ::: ::: **Global Options** Instead of repeating options in every chunk, set them once at the beginning of your document. ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.callout-note} Chunk options affect a **single chunk**, while global options become the **default for every chunk** in the document. ::: **Inline Code** Inline code inserts **individual values** directly into your narrative. Instead of typing: > We enrolled **53940** participants. Use: ```markdown We enrolled 53940 participants. ``` which renders as: > We enrolled **53940** participants. Another example: ```markdown The average diamond price was $3,932.80. ``` renders as: > The average diamond price was **$3,933**. ::: notes **Why use inline code?** If your data change, your text updates automatically the next time you render the document. This eliminates copy-and-paste errors and helps keep reports reproducible. How many of you have ever updated a figure but forgotten to update the number in the paragraph above it? Inline code solves exactly that problem. ::: ## Figures and Tables Insert example of figure and table here provide the following examples: set eval to false - code set eval to true - name plot ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](communicate_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: notes Why figures/tables in Quarto? Traditional: - create - save - copy - paste Quarto: - update code - render ::: ## YAML **Overview** incorporate this section from mb's notes **Styling Extensions** **Citations** ## Troubleshooting Common errors include: - missing package - YAML spacing - missing parentheses - unclosed chunks ::: {.callout-tip} Useful debugging advice includes: 1. Read the error 2. Find the line 3. Fix one thing 4. Render again ::: ## Chapter 28 Summary # Chapter 29: Formats ::: notes Core idea: One source → many outputs ::: ## Output options **Documents** - pdf - makes a PDF with LaTeX - docx - for Microsoft Word **Presentations** - revealjs - HTML presentation - pptx - Powerpoint presentation ## Interactivity **Shiny apps** ## Chapter 29 Summary Potential uses: - study reports - MRI summaries - grant updates - recruitment tracking - conference presentations ::: notes Highligh Brian's Disclosure report Give an example of a use case for my lab. Ask: What other use cases can you think of? ::: ## Best Practices It is best practice to save and review often. - render often - keep files organized - write narrative - document decisions - embrace reproducibility ## Wrap-Up Quarto helps us: - communicate - reproduce - automate - collaborate - publish Now let's build a Quarto presentation. # Time to Practice!

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
